correctness.rationale: Direct reconstruction of four independent Rademacher BKS probes and two leave-one-out XDiag probes yields exact all-sign risk formulas. The denominator is a product of strictly positive image norms. The cubic threshold is shown unique by a derivative sign argument. A finite discrete-support continuity argument proves high-dimensional opposite risk advantages. The standalone Python 3 exact-rational verifier passed 1208 assertion families, including complete two-sign-pair enumeration and relevant exact identities.

value.rationale: At equal matvec cost, an exact two-dimensional classification distinguishes spectral anisotropy and correlation strength and provides a sharp one-crossing criterion for when deflation-based diagonal estimation is worthwhile. Both methods have arbitrarily severe relative risk failures on strictly positive-definite high-dimensional inputs, so no uniform dominance can be inferred from their unbiasedness or broad experimental rankings. The result is a substantive boundary for algorithm selection, though not a general-purpose complexity theorem.
